common_name: Rob's Boolaroo African Violet (Semiminiature Trailing Pink Fantasy Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Bred by Ralph Robinson at The Violet Barn and registered with AVSA (#8053), Rob's Boolaroo is one of the grower's own trailing hybrids.

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Rob's Boolaroo is a semiminiature trailing cultivar that branches from multiple crowns rather than forming a single rosette, bearing sparkling double light-pink flowers heavily peppered with blue fantasy speckling over a constant, heavy bloom cycle; grow it in a hanging pot or wide shallow container to show off its cascading habit. Water carefully to avoid wetting the crown and leaves, feed every four weeks with a balanced fertilizer formulated for African violets, and groom side shoots only as needed since multiple crowns are part of its intended trailing growth rather than a fault.
sources: The Violet Barn — Ralph Robinson cultivar descriptions

common_name: Rob's Twinkle Blue African Violet (Miniature Near-Black-Leaved Blue Semibell Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Bred by Ralph Robinson at The Violet Barn and registered with AVSA (#8616), this miniature matures at barely 2-3 inches across.

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Rob's Twinkle Blue is a true miniature, maturing at barely 2-3 inches across, with semi-double deep-blue semibell flowers held over very tiny, nearly-black foliage that gives striking contrast to the profuse blue blooms. Its diminutive scale makes it a favorite for thimble pots and collector displays, but also means overwatering and over-fertilizing do more damage than with larger cultivars; water carefully and feed at diluted strength appropriate for its tiny root system, rotating the pot periodically for even growth.
sources: The Violet Barn — Ralph Robinson cultivar descriptions

common_name: Rob's Argyle Socks African Violet (Semiminiature Crown-Variegated Fantasy Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Bred by Ralph Robinson at The Violet Barn and registered with AVSA (#8808).

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Rob's Argyle Socks is a semiminiature cultivar prized as much for its foliage as its bloom, carrying dark green and beige crown-variegated leaves beneath large, semi-double pale pink star flowers frosted with blue fantasy markings. Variegated African violets like this one color best under bright, consistent light and cooler growing temperatures, and benefit from lighter feeding than solid-green cultivars since excess nitrogen can push variegated leaves back toward plain green. Water carefully to avoid wetting the crown and rotate the pot regularly for symmetrical growth.
sources: The Violet Barn — Ralph Robinson cultivar descriptions

common_name: Rob's Love Bite African Violet (Miniature Deep Red Variegated Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Bred by Ralph Robinson at The Violet Barn and registered with AVSA (#9039); described by the breeder as their best red.

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Rob's Love Bite is a miniature cultivar bearing reddest-red, semi-double pansy-form flowers over dark, variegated foliage that tends toward pink variegation rather than white under strong grow-light conditions. Give it bright, even light to hold both the flower color and the leaf variegation, water carefully to avoid wetting the crown and leaves, and feed lightly with a fertilizer formulated for African violets, since heavier feeding can push variegated foliage back toward solid green.

common_name: Rob's Astro Zombie African Violet (Miniature Blue-Purple Fantasy Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Bred by Ralph Robinson at The Violet Barn and registered with AVSA (#10138).

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Rob's Astro Zombie is a prolific-blooming miniature carrying semi-double deep blue-to-purple star flowers dusted with bright rose-pink fantasy puffs, held over dark, compact foliage. It is a hardy, easy grower but suckers freely from the crown, so pinch off extra growing points regularly to keep a single, well-formed rosette rather than a crowded multi-crown plant. Water carefully to avoid wetting the crown and leaves and feed every four weeks with a balanced fertilizer formulated for African violets.

common_name: Rob's Galiwinku African Violet (Award-Winning Semiminiature Trailing Orchid Fantasy Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Bred by Ralph Robinson at The Violet Barn and registered with AVSA (#8059); named Best in Show at the 2013 AVSA Convention and the winningest trailer in the country in 2003.

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Rob's Galiwinku is a vigorous, constantly blooming semiminiature trailer bearing double orchid-colored flowers overlaid with dark blue fantasy markings; it has won top trailing-class show awards, including Best in Show at the 2013 AVSA Convention. Grow it in a wide, shallow pot or hanging basket to let the multiple crowns cascade, water carefully to avoid wetting the foliage, and feed every four weeks with a balanced fertilizer formulated for African violets.
sources: The Violet Barn — Ralph Robinson cultivar descriptions

common_name: Rob's Humpty Doo African Violet (Semiminiature Trailing White Striped Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Bred at The Violet Barn and registered with AVSA (#8456).

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Rob's Humpty Doo is an extremely profuse semiminiature trailer with semi-double white flowers marked by blue side stripes on each petal, held over glossy medium-green foliage; growers report it in near-constant bloom once established. Grow it in a hanging pot or wide shallow container to display the cascading multi-crown habit, water carefully to avoid wetting the crown and leaves, and feed every four weeks with a balanced fertilizer formulated for African violets.

common_name: Rob's Vanilla Trail African Violet (Semiminiature Trailing Cream Double Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Bred at The Violet Barn and registered with AVSA (#9296).

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Rob's Vanilla Trail bears fully double, cream-to-blush-white flowers over very dark, serrated, quilted semiminiature foliage, forming an easy-growing, constantly blooming trailer well suited to a hanging basket or wide shallow pot where its cascading multiple crowns can spread. Water carefully to avoid wetting the crown and leaves, feed every four weeks with a balanced fertilizer formulated for African violets, and let side crowns develop rather than removing them, since a full, spreading habit is the point of a trailing cultivar.

common_name: Rob's Boondoggle African Violet (Semiminiature Red and White Ruffled Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Bred by Ralph Robinson at The Violet Barn and registered with AVSA (#7880).

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Rob's Boondoggle is a semiminiature cultivar with semi-double deep red star flowers edged in a wide, ruffled white border, set off by wavy, nearly-black foliage. It is a heavy, reliable bloomer that often arrives in bud, so grow it under bright indirect light with careful watering that avoids wetting the crown, and feed every four weeks with a balanced fertilizer formulated for African violets to sustain repeat bloom cycles.

common_name: Warm Sunshine African Violet (Award-Winning Standard Double Yellow Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Hybridized by Sorano and registered with AVSA (#9546); named Best New Cultivar at the 2004 AVSA convention.

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Warm Sunshine is a standard-sized cultivar bred by Sorano, carrying double, soft yellow star flowers with darker yellow streaks over medium-to-dark green foliage that is sometimes lightly mottled; it was named Best New Cultivar at the 2004 AVSA convention and remains one of the most popular yellow-flowered violets in cultivation. True yellow flower tones develop best when the plant is grown on the cool side with bright, even light; warmer conditions can shift the bloom color toward a warm white. Feed every four weeks with a balanced fertilizer formulated for African violets and water carefully to avoid wetting the crown and leaves.

common_name: Melodie Kimi African Violet (Standard White Sticktite Pansy-Form Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks. Registered with the African Violet Society of America on September 15, 1994, as a standard (Western) cultivar.

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Melodie Kimi is a standard-sized, AVSA-registered cultivar with single, white sticktite pansy-form flowers whose top petals carry purple-blue tips, held over medium green, plain, quilted, wavy foliage typical of Western-type standard violets. Grow under 12 to 14 hours of bright, indirect light daily for full bloom, water carefully to avoid wetting the crown and leaves, and feed every four weeks with a balanced fertilizer formulated for African violets, removing spent flower stems to encourage repeat blooming.
sources: African Violet Society of America — plant registration database
